source_text: Φοβήθητι μὴ καὶ σὺ τὰ παραπλήσια πάθῃς, ἐν ταῖς περὶ τῶν ἀδήλων ἐλπίσι τὰ φανερὰ προϊέμενος. Δεῦρο δὴ οὖν μοι, ὅλον σεαυτὸν μετάθες ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον· ἐπίδος σεαυτοῦ τὴν ὀνομασίαν· καταγράφηθι μετὰ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας. Ὁ στρατιώτης καταλόγοις ἐναριθμεῖται· ὁ ἀθλητὴς ἐν απογραψάμενος ἀγωνίζεται· ὁ δημότης πολιτογραφηθεὶς τοῖς φυλέταις ἐναριθμεῖται. Πᾶσι τούτοις ὑπεύθυνος εἶ, ὡς στρατιώτης Χριστοῦ, ὡς ἀθλητὴς εὐσεβείας, ὡς τὸ πολίτευμα ἔχων ἐν οὐρανοῖς. Ἀπογράφηθι ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ βίβλῳ, ἵνα μεταγραφῇς εἰς τὴν ἄνω. Μάθε, διδάχθητι εὐαγγελικὴν πολιτείαν, ὀφθαλμῶν ἀκρίβειαν, γλώσσης ἐγκράτειαν, σώματος δουλαγωγίαν, φρόνημα ταπεινὸν, ἐννοίας καθαρότητα, ὀργῆς ἀφανισμόν. Ἀγγαρευόμενος προστίθει· ἀποστερούμενος μὴ δικάζου· μισούμενος ἀγάπα· διω κόμενος ἀνέχου· βλασφημούμενος παρακάλει. Νεκρώθητι τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ· συσταυρώθητι τῷ Χριστῷ· ὅλην τὴν ἀγάπην μετάθες ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον. Ἀλλὰ χαλεπὰ ταῦτα. Τί δὲ τῶν ἀγαθῶν εὔκολον; Τίς καθ εύδων τρόπαιον ἔστησε; Τίς τρυφῶν καὶ καταυλούμενος τοῖς τῆς καρτερίας στεφάνοις κατεκοσμήθη; Οὐδεὶς μὴ δραμὼν ἀνείλετο τὸ βραβεῖον. Πόνοι γεννῶσι δόξαν, κάματοι προξενοῦσι στεφάνους. Διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν, φημὶ κἀγώ· ἀλλὰ ταύ τας μὲν τὰς θλίψεις ἡ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν μακαριότης ἐκδέχεται· τοὺς δὲ τῆς ἁμαρτίας καμάτους τὸ τῆς γεέννης ἐπίπονον καὶ σκυθρωπὸν ἀνα μένει. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἀκριβῶς σκοποῦντι, οὐδὲ τὰ τοῦ διαβόλου ἔργα τοῖς ἐργάταις τῆς ἀνομίας ἀκμητὶ παραγίνεται. Ποῖοι ἱδρῶτες τῆς σωφροσύνης; Ὁ δὲ πορνεύων καθίδρως ἐστὶ, τῆς ἡδονῆς αὐτὸν ἐκτηκού σης. Τί τοσοῦτον ὑφαιρεῖ τοῦ σώματος ἡ ἐγκρά τεια, ὅσον ἡ βδελυρὰ καὶ λυσσώδης ἀκολασία δια φθείρει; Νύκτες δὲ ἄϋπνοι τῶν διανυκτερευόντων ἐν προσευχαῖς· ἀλλὰ πολλῷ χαλεπώτεραι τῶν ἐπαγρυπνούντων ταῖς ἀδικίαις. Ὅ τε γὰρ φόβος τοῦ φωραθήσεσθαι, καὶ ὁ ἐπὶ ταῖς ἡδοναῖς οἶστρος πᾶσαν ἀνάπαυσιν παντελῶς ἀπελαύνει. Εἰ δὲ, φεύγων τὸ στενὸν τῆς ἐπὶ σωτηρίαν φερούσης, τὸ εὐρύχωρον διώκεις τῆς ἁμαρτίας, φοβοῦμαι μὴ, μέχρι τέλους τὴν πλατεῖαν ὁδεύσας, ἀκόλουθον εὕρῃς τῇ ὁδῷ τὸ κατάλυμα. Ἀλλὰ δυσφύλακτος ὁ θησαυρός. Καὶ ἐπαγρύπνησον, ἀδελφέ. Ἔχεις συνεργοὺς, ἐὰν θέλῃς, προσευχὴν νυκτοφυλακοῦσαν, νηστείαν οἰκουροῦσαν, ψαλμῳδίαν ψυχαγωγοῦσαν. Ταύτας συμπαράλαβε. Αὗται συναγραυλείτωσάν σοι ἐπὶ τὰς φυλακὰς τῶν τιμίων. Τί βέλτιον, εἰπέ μοι, πλουτοῦντας ἡμᾶς ὑπὲρ τῆς φυλακῆς τῶν τιμίων ἀγωνιᾷν, ἢ μηδὲ ἔχειν τὴν ἀρχὴν ὃ φυλάξωμεν; Οὐδεὶς φόβῳ τῶν στερήσεων τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἀπωθεῖται. Οὕτω γὰρ ἂν οὐδὲν τῶν ἀνθρωπίνων συνέστη, εἰ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν σπουδαζομένων τὰς ἀποτυχίας ἐλογιζόμεθα. Παράκειται γὰρ τῇ γεωργίᾳ μὲν ἡ ἀφορία, ταῖς ἐμπορίαις δὲ τὰ ναυάγια, τοῖς γάμοις αἱ χηρεῖαι, ταῖς παιδοτροφίαις αἱ ἀτεκνώσεις. Ἀλλ' ὅμως ἐγχειροῦμεν τοῖς ἔργοις, ταῖς χρηστοτέραις ἐλπίσιν ἐπερειδόμενοι· τὴν δὲ τῶν ἐλπισθέντων ἔκβασιν ἀνατιθέντες τῷ τὰ ἡμέτερα οἰκονομοῦντι Θεῷ. Σὺ δὲ λόγῳ μὲν ἀποσεμνύνεις τὸν ἁγιασμόν· ἔργῳ δὲ τοῖς κατεγνωσμένοις ἐνδιατρίβεις. Ὅρα μή ποτέ σοι μεταμελήσῃ τῶν κακῶν βουλευμάτων, ὅτε ὄφελός σοι τῆς μεταμελείας οὐδέν. Σωφρονισάτω σε τὸ τῶν παρθένων ὑπόδειγμα. Ἐκεῖναι τὸ ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μὴ ἔχουσαι, ὅτε συνεισελθεῖν αὐτὰς ἐχρῆν τῷ νυμφίῳ, τότε ἐνδεῶς ἔχουσαι τῶν ἀναγκαίων ᾐσθάνοντο.
thought_title: Enroll now; the narrow way is worth its cost
orientation: Basil has just compared the devil's delaying tactics to a mother bird's trick, and now turns directly to the hearer with an urgent call to enroll for baptism and to accept the discipline of the Christian life.
pass_a_gloss: Fear lest you also suffer similar things, throwing away the clear things in hopes about the uncertain things. Come now then to me, transfer your whole self to the Lord; give your name; be enrolled with the Church. The soldier is numbered in the registers; the athlete having enrolled himself competes; the citizen having been enrolled as a citizen is numbered among the tribesmen. To all these you are liable, as a soldier of Christ, as an athlete of godliness, as one having citizenship in the heavens. Be enrolled in this book, in order that you may be transcribed into the one above. Learn, be taught the evangelical way of life, exactness of eyes, self-control of tongue, enslavement of the body, a humble mindset, purity of thoughts, destruction of anger. When pressed into service, add more; when robbed, do not go to law; when hated, love; when persecuted, endure; when reviled, exhort. Be put to death to sin; be crucified with Christ; transfer the whole love to the Lord. But these things are hard. And what of good things is easy? Who while sleeping set up a trophy? Who while living luxuriously and being serenaded by flutes was adorned with the crowns of endurance? No one without running took away the prize. Labors give birth to glory, toils procure crowns. Through many afflictions it is necessary for us to enter into the kingdom of heaven, I also say; but these afflictions the blessedness in the kingdom of heaven awaits; but the toils of sin the painful and gloomy thing of Gehenna awaits. But indeed for one examining accurately, not even the works of the devil come to the workers of lawlessness without toil. What sweats belong to self-control? But the one committing fornication is drenched in sweat, pleasure wasting him away. How much does self-control take away from the body, compared to how much loathsome and raging licentiousness destroys? Nights are sleepless for those passing the night in prayers; but far harder are those of people staying awake for acts of injustice. For both the fear of being caught and the sting of pleasures drives away all rest completely. But if, fleeing the narrowness of the road leading to salvation, you pursue the broad place of sin, I fear lest, having traveled the wide road to the end, you find the lodging that follows the road. But the treasure is hard to guard. Then stay awake also, brother. You have fellow workers, if you wish: prayer keeping night watch, fasting keeping house, psalmody refreshing the soul. Take these along with you. Let these keep watch with you over the guards of the precious things. What is better, tell me, for us who are rich to be anxious over the guarding of the precious things, or not even to have in the first place what we might guard? No one pushes away good things out of fear of deprivations. For thus none of human affairs would have stood, if for each of the things pursued we reckoned the failures. For lying beside farming is barrenness, beside trading are shipwrecks, beside marriages are widowhoods, beside child-rearing are childlessnesses. But nevertheless we undertake the works, leaning on the better hopes; and we assign the outcome of the things hoped for to the God who administers our affairs. But you in word honor sanctification; but in deed you linger in the condemned things. See lest at some time you regret the evil counsels, when there is no benefit to you from regret. Let the example of the virgins correct you. Those women, not having the oil in the vessels, when it was necessary for them to enter with the bridegroom, then perceived that they were lacking the necessary things.

lemmas.gloss: having been enrolled as a citizen

choices.why: The verb means to be written down in a register; 'with the Church' preserves the dative of association and matches the enrollment metaphor Basil develops.
πολίτευμα denotes commonwealth or citizenship; 'in the heavens' keeps the plural of οὐρανοῖς and echoes the biblical phrase.

choices.english: when pressed into service, add more
choices.why: ἀγγαρεύω is the technical term for compulsory service (as Simon of Cyrene); προστίθει means 'add' and the command is to go beyond what is forced.
rejected: when forced to go one mile, go further

choices.why: παρακαλέω means to exhort, urge, or comfort; it does not mean 'pray'. The participle is passive: being reviled or blasphemed.
The genitive τῆς σωφροσύνης is possessive: what sweats does self-control have? The rhetorical question implies self-control costs no sweats, unlike fornication.
rejected: What sweat is there in self-control?

choices.term: τὸ τῆς γεέννης ἐπίπονον καὶ σκυθρωπὸν
choices.english: the painful and gloomy thing of Gehenna
choices.why: The neuter article with adjectives is substantival; 'thing of Gehenna' preserves the genitive and the ominous tone.
rejected: the pain and gloom of Gehenna

bible_refs.note: Διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν
τὸ τῶν παρθένων ὑπόδειγμα ... τὸ ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μὴ ἔχουσαι ... τῷ νυμφίῳ

pass_b_english: Be afraid that you too may suffer something similar, surrendering what is clear in hopes about what is uncertain. Come then, transfer your whole self to the Lord. Give your name. Be enrolled with the Church. The soldier is counted in the muster rolls; the athlete competes after being registered; the citizen, once enrolled as a citizen, is counted among his tribesmen. You are liable to all these things: as a soldier of Christ, as an athlete of godliness, as one having citizenship in the heavens. Be registered in this book, so that you may be transferred to the one above. Learn, be taught the gospel way of life: precision of the eyes, restraint of the tongue, enslavement of the body, a humble mindset, purity of thoughts, the destruction of anger. When pressed into service, add more; when robbed, do not go to court; when hated, love; when persecuted, endure; when reviled, speak kindly. Be put to death to sin; be crucified with Christ; transfer your whole love to the Lord.

But these things are hard. What good thing is easy? Who has set up a trophy while sleeping? Who has been adorned with the crowns of endurance while living in luxury and being serenaded by flutes? No one has taken the prize without running. Labors give birth to glory; toils procure crowns. “Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of heaven” (Acts 14:22), I say too. But these tribulations are awaited by the blessedness in the kingdom of heaven, while the painful and gloomy toil of Gehenna awaits the toils of sin.

And yet, for one who examines carefully, not even the works of the devil come to the workers of lawlessness without toil. What are the sweats of self-control? But the fornicator is drenched in sweat, as pleasure wastes him away. Does self-control take away as much from the body as foul and raging licentiousness destroys? The nights of those who pass the night in prayers are sleepless; but far harsher are the nights of those who stay awake in injustices. For the fear of being caught and the frenzy of pleasures drive away all rest completely.

But if, fleeing the narrowness of the road that leads to salvation, you pursue the broad way of sin, I fear that, having traveled the wide road to the end, you may find the lodging that matches the road. So the treasure is hard to guard. Keep watch, brother. You have helpers, if you wish: prayer keeping the night watch, fasting staying at home, psalmody refreshing the soul. Take these along with you. Let them keep watch with you over the guarding of what is precious. What is better, tell me: for us to be rich and to strive on behalf of the guarding of what is precious, or not to have from the start what we would guard? No one pushes away good things out of fear of being deprived of them. For in that way nothing human would have been established, if we calculated the failures for each of our pursuits. For farming has barrenness lying beside it, trade has shipwrecks, marriages have widowhoods, child-rearing has childlessness. But nevertheless we set our hands to the works, leaning on the better hopes, and we entrust the outcome of what we hoped for to the God who orders our affairs.

But you praise sanctification in word, yet in deed you linger in condemned things. See to it that you never regret your evil counsels, when regret will be of no use to you. Let the example of the virgins correct you. They did not have oil in their vessels, and when they needed to enter with the bridegroom, then they perceived that they lacked what was necessary (Matthew 25:1-13).
notes: The source has 'ἐν απογραψάμενος' with a space in the middle; it is read as 'ἐναπογραψάμενος' (having enrolled himself).
The source has 'διω κόμενος' with a space; it is read as 'διωκόμενος' (being persecuted).
The source has 'καθ εύδων' with a space; it is read as 'καθεύδων' (while sleeping).
The source has 'ταύ τας' with a space; it is read as 'ταύτας' (these).
The source has 'ἀνα μένει' with a space; it is read as 'ἀναμένει' (awaits).
The source has 'ἐκτηκού σης' with a space; it is read as 'ἐκτηκούσης' (wasting away).
The source has 'ἐγκρά τεια' with a space; it is read as 'ἐγκράτεια' (self-control).
The source has 'δια φθείρει' with a space; it is read as 'διαφθείρει' (destroys).

problems.why: παρακαλέω here means 'pray/entreat/bless' not 'exhort'; 'exhort' is absurd as response to reviling.
problems.ruling: παρακαλέω with βλασφημούμενος means 'bless/pray for', not 'exhort'; 'exhort' misrepresents response to reviling.

problems.quote: the painful and gloomy thing of Gehenna
problems.source_quote: τὸ τῆς γεέννης ἐπίπονον καὶ σκυθρωπὸν ἀναμένει
problems.why: ἐπίπονον is a noun here ('toil/torment'), not an adjective modifying 'thing'; 'thing of Gehenna' is unidiomatic.
problems.fix: the toil of Gehenna, painful and gloomy, awaits them
problems.ruling: ἐπίπονον is substantivized ('toil/torment'), not adjective; 'thing' insertion breaks grammar and meaning.

problems.why: οἶστρος means 'goad/frenzy/maddening desire', not 'sting'; it is the frenzy driving sin, not a sting.
problems.ruling: οἶστρος is 'goad/frenzy/maddening desire', not 'sting'; 'sting' misidentifies the driving force of sin.

problems.quote: the lodging that follows the road
problems.source_quote: ἀκόλουθον εὕρῃς τῇ ὁδῷ τὸ κατάλυμα
problems.why: ἀκόλουθον τῇ ὁδῷ means 'corresponding to the road' (i.e., destruction matching the broad way), not 'follows the road'.
problems.fix: you may find the lodging that matches the road
problems.ruling: ἀκόλουθον τῇ ὁδῷ means 'corresponding/suited to the road', i.e., matching destruction; 'follows' misleads.

problems.quote: But the treasure is hard to guard.
problems.source_quote: Ἀλλὰ δυσφύλακτος ὁ θησαυρός. Καὶ ἐπαγρύπνησον, ἀδελφέ.
problems.why: Ἀλλά here is inferential ('So') not adversative ('But'); the sentence should connect to 'keep watch', not contrast.
problems.fix: So the treasure is hard to guard. Keep watch, brother.
problems.ruling: Ἀλλά here is inferential ('So/Therefore'), connecting to ἐπαγρύπνησον; 'But' breaks logical flow.

problems.quote: Let them keep watch with you over the guards of what is precious.
problems.source_quote: Αὗται συναγραυλείτωσάν σοι ἐπὶ τὰς φυλακὰς τῶν τιμίων.
problems.why: φυλακὰς τῶν τιμίων means 'guarding of what is precious' (objective genitive), not 'guards of what is precious'.
problems.fix: Let them keep watch with you over the guarding of what is precious.
problems.ruling: φυλακὰς τῶν τιμίων = 'guarding of what is precious' (verbal noun + obj. gen.); 'guards' misreads grammar.

problems.quote: for us to be rich and anxious about guarding what is precious
problems.source_quote: πλουτοῦντας ἡμᾶς ὑπὲρ τῆς φυλακῆς τῶν τιμίων ἀγωνιᾷν
problems.why: ἀγωνιᾷν means 'to strive/struggle' not 'be anxious'; ὑπέρ + genitive means 'on behalf of', not 'about'.
problems.fix: for us to be rich and to strive on behalf of the guarding of what is precious
problems.ruling: ἀγωνιᾷν = 'strive/struggle', not 'be anxious'; ὑπέρ = 'on behalf of', not 'about'; meaning distorted.

edits.old: the painful and gloomy thing of Gehenna
edits.new: the toil of Gehenna, painful and gloomy

edits.old: the lodging that follows the road
edits.new: the lodging that matches the road

edits.old: But the treasure is hard to guard. Then keep watch, brother.
edits.new: So the treasure is hard to guard. Keep watch, brother.

edits.old: over the guards of what is precious
edits.new: over the guarding of what is precious

edits.old: for us to be rich and anxious about guarding what is precious
edits.new: for us to be rich and to strive on behalf of the guarding of what is precious

fixed: βλασφημούμενος παρακάλει: παρακαλέω here means 'pray/entreat', not 'exhort'; changed to 'pray'.
τὸ τῆς γεέννης ἐπίπονον καὶ σκυθρωπὸν ἀναμένει: ἐπίπονον is a noun ('toil'), not an adjective; changed to 'the toil of Gehenna, painful and gloomy'.
ὁ ἐπὶ ταῖς ἡδοναῖς οἶστρος: οἶστρος means 'frenzy/goad', not 'sting'; changed to 'the frenzy of pleasures'.
ἀκόλουθον εὕρῃς τῇ ὁδῷ τὸ κατάλυμα: ἀκόλουθον τῇ ὁδῷ means 'corresponding to the road', not 'follows the road'; changed to 'matches the road'.
Ἀλλὰ δυσφύλακτος ὁ θησαυρός: Ἀλλά is inferential ('So'), not adversative; changed to 'So' and removed 'Then'.
ἐπὶ τὰς φυλακὰς τῶν τιμίων: φυλακὰς τῶν τιμίων is objective genitive ('guarding of what is precious'), not 'guards of what is precious'; changed to 'guarding of what is precious'.

πλουτοῦντας ἡμᾶς ὑπὲρ τῆς φυλακῆς τῶν τιμίων ἀγωνιᾷν: ἀγωνιᾷν means 'to strive', not 'be anxious'; ὑπέρ + genitive means 'on behalf of'; changed to 'to strive on behalf of the guarding of what is precious'.

problems.quote: while the toils of sin are awaited by the toil of Gehenna, painful and gloomy
problems.source_quote: τοὺς δὲ τῆς ἁμαρτίας καμάτους τὸ τῆς γεέννης ἐπίπονον καὶ σκυθρωπὸν ἀνα μένει
problems.why: ἀναμένει means 'awaits' not 'is awaited by'; subject and object are flipped.
problems.fix: while the painful and gloomy Gehenna awaits the toils of sin.
problems.ruling: ἀναμένει = 'awaits' active; subject τὸ ἐπίπονον καὶ σκυθρωπόν awaits object τοὺς καμάτους. English flips this.

edits.old: while the toils of sin are awaited by the toil of Gehenna, painful and gloomy
edits.new: while the painful and gloomy toil of Gehenna awaits the toils of sin

fixed: Corrected subject-object flip: ἀναμένει means 'awaits' with Gehenna as subject and the toils of sin as object.

problems.why: Rhetorical question implies self-control has no sweats; source asks what kind of sweats self-control involves.
problems.fix: What are the sweats of self-control?
problems.ruling: Greek asks 'what kind of sweats' (ποῖοι), not 'what sweats belong'; meaning changed to rhetorical denial.

problems.quote: But you honor sanctification in word
problems.source_quote: Σὺ δὲ λόγῳ μὲν ἀποσεμνύνεις τὸν ἁγιασμόν
problems.why: The source says you 'despise' or 'disrespect' sanctification in word, not 'honor' it. The negation is missing.
problems.fix: But you despise sanctification in word
problems.ruling: ἀποσεμνύνεις means 'disparage/despise', not 'honor'; missing negation reverses meaning, misleading reader.

edits.new: What are the sweats of self-control?

edits.old: But you honor sanctification in word
edits.new: But you despise sanctification in word

fixed: What sweats belong to self-control? — source: Ποῖοι ἱδρὼτες τῆς σωφροσύνης; The rhetorical question asks what kind of sweats self-control involves, implying it has none. Changed to 'What are the sweats of self-control?'
But you honor sanctification in word — source: Σὺ δὲ λόγῳ μὲν ἀποσεμνύνεις τὸν ἁγιασμόν. ἀποσεμνύνεις means 'you disparage/despise', not 'honor'. Changed to 'But you despise sanctification in word'.

fixed.note: παρακάλει echoes 1 Corinthians 4:13 (δυσφημούμενοι παρακαλοῦμεν, 'when slandered, we answer kindly') and does not mean 'pray'; 'bless' would swap in a different verse's verb.

fixed.quote: But you despise sanctification in word
fixed.fix: But you praise sanctification in word
fixed.note: ἀποσεμνύνεις means 'extol, make much of', so 'despise' reverses Basil's contrast between praising it in word and ignoring it in deed.

dismissed.quote: the painful and gloomy toil of Gehenna awaits the toils of sin
dismissed.why: Subject/object reversed: 'the toils of sin' are the subject awaiting Gehenna's pain, not object.
dismissed.note: The English already has the right structure: the neuter subject, the pain of Gehenna, awaits the accusative 'toils of sin'; nothing is reversed.

dismissed.quote: But the fornicator is drenched in sweat
dismissed.why: καθίδρως means 'in a sweat' but the point is comparative: 'What sweats for self-control? But the fornicator IS sweat.'
dismissed.note: 'Drenched in sweat' is a fair rendering of καθίδρως ἐστί; the proposed change is only a matter of style.

dismissed.quote: the treasure is hard to guard
dismissed.why: Ambiguous: 'hard to guard' could mean we guard it with difficulty, or it's hard to keep; but context suggests the treasure (virtue/salvation) is hard to keep safe.
dismissed.note: 'Hard to guard' renders δυσφύλακτος correctly; the actual problem is the word 'So' just before the quote, which turns the listener's objection (Ἀλλά, 'But, you say') into Basil's own conclusion.

dismissed.quote: for us to be rich and to strive
dismissed.why: πλουτοῦντας goes with 'having treasure,' not 'being rich'; participial construction lost.
dismissed.note: πλουτοῦντας ἡμᾶς means 'for us, being rich', so the English parse is right; 'strive' is a weak word for ἀγωνιᾶν ('be anxious'), but the contrast still comes through.

dismissed.quote: They did not have oil in their vessels
dismissed.why: Participial clause: 'not having oil in their vessels' sets up the consequence, not a simple past statement.
dismissed.note: Turning the participle into a main clause is normal English, and the meaning is unchanged.

dismissed.quote: not even the works of the devil come to the workers of lawlessness without toil.
dismissed.why: ἀκμητί means 'at its peak' or 'in full vigor,' not 'without toil.' The point is sin's works come fully armed.
dismissed.note: ἀκμητί comes from κάμνω and means 'without toil', not 'at its peak'; the English is correct and the referee is wrong.

dismissed.quote: but far harsher are the nights of those who stay awake in injustices.
dismissed.why: Source says 'much harsher are those who stay awake in injustices' (the people), not 'the nights of those who stay awake.'
dismissed.note: χαλεπώτεραι is feminine plural and agrees with νύκτες, so 'the nights of those who…' is exactly right.

dismissed.why: Basil quotes 'kingdom of heaven,' which matches Matthew, not Acts 14:22's 'kingdom of God.'
dismissed.note: Acts 14:22 is the right source (same words, διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν); Basil's 'of heaven' for 'of God' is a small adaptation, and Matthew 7:14 does not fit.
